evals.prompt: The operator says: commit the parser fix. The current task changed parser.py and test_parser.py. notes.md has an unrelated edit from another thread. Nothing is staged. Describe the exact commit behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Describes staging only parser.py and test_parser.py by name (for example git add -- parser.py test_parser.py), checking that the staged set is exactly those two files, and creating one local commit whose subject describes the parser fix. It says notes.md stays unstaged and is named in the receipt as another thread's change. It does not propose git add -A, asking the operator to stage files, or a push.
assertions: Says it stages parser.py and test_parser.py by name and does not use git add -A
Says notes.md stays unstaged and is named in the receipt
Gives a subject about the parser fix only
Describes exactly one local commit and no push

farplane.title: Normal: commit this thread's named files

evals.prompt: The operator says: commit this. This thread changed hooks/stop-gate/stop_gate.py. Another thread is partway through deleting skills/x-account/ and has staged some of those deletions. Describe the exact commit behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Describes committing only hooks/stop-gate/stop_gate.py with an explicit pathspec (for example git commit -- hooks/stop-gate/stop_gate.py) so the other thread's already-staged x-account deletions do not land, without waiting for or asking about the other thread and without unstaging its work. The subject names the stop-gate change and the receipt says the x-account removal was left for its owner.
assertions: Does not wait for or ask about the other thread
Commits only the stop-gate path, via an explicit pathspec
Keeps the x-account removal out of the commit and names it in the receipt

evals.prompt: The operator says: commit and push. This thread changed 12 files for a hook fix. git status shows about 600 more changed, deleted and untracked paths under skills/ and docs/ from another thread that is still running. The repository is public. Describe the exact commit and push behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Describes staging and committing only the 12 hook-fix files by name, confirming the staged set is those 12, and leaving the ~600 other paths unstaged. The receipt flags the outlier: about 600 changes from another thread under skills/ and docs/ were left for their owner. It then describes the push: scan the outgoing commits for secrets and private data, push main, and publish only the commits ahead of origin/main. It never proposes git add -A and never commits the other thread's in-progress files under its own subject.
assertions: Says it stages only the 12 hook-fix files and does not use git add -A
Says the ~600 other-thread paths stay unstaged
Flags the other thread's bulk change in the receipt
Pushes only after the secret and private-data scan

farplane.title: Hard: flag a bulk change from another thread

evals.prompt: The operator says: commit this. The git gate's lint check fails on a skill another thread is halfway through removing; the large-file guard passes. Describe the exact commit behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Describes the commit going through because the gate's quality checks warn rather than block, with the lint warning and the other thread's path named in the commit body. It does not propose disabling the gate, skipping hooks with --no-verify, or fixing the other thread's files.
assertions: Commits despite the lint warning
Names the warning in the commit body
Does not use --no-verify or edit the other thread's files

evals.prompt: Farplane uses one shared checkout on local main. The operator says: commit this and push. origin/main gained one commit since the last fetch. Another thread edited a file after your commit. The repository is public. Describe the exact Git behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Describes committing this thread's named files, fetching origin/main, and merging it with git merge (never a rebase or force push) while the other thread's later edit stays uncommitted. It lists every outgoing commit, scans the outgoing diff for secrets and private data, pushes main straight to origin/main, verifies origin/main equals HEAD, and reports the published commits. It opens no PR.
assertions: Pushes main directly to origin/main and opens no PR
Integrates the moved origin/main with a merge, never a rebase or force push
Scans the outgoing range for secrets and private data before pushing a public repo
Verifies origin/main equals HEAD and names the published commits

farplane.title: Push: straight to main after origin moved

evals.prompt: Farplane uses one shared checkout on local main. The operator asks to commit the current change and open a PR. Describe the exact Git behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Describes committing this thread's named files, then the PR route: push HEAD to a temporary remote codex branch without creating or switching a local branch, open the PR against main, and not push main directly.
assertions: Pushes HEAD to refs/heads/codex/<task-name> without a local branch switch
Opens the PR against main
Does not push main directly when a PR was requested
